sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 combines the title, the key map of the whole town at 700 ft to an inch, the water and fire department notes and the street index with a map strip at 100 ft to an inch along the eastern edge of Westmont in Haddon Township. Only that map strip is covered here: an L-shaped area left of and below the heavy line. Along its west side run the Pennsylvania Railroad's Delaware River Bridge Route and Windsor Avenue (Road), which in the upper part bends north-east and is crossed by Utica Avenue, with blocks G and H and the Nelson Johnson Cement Block Company beside the tracks. The lower part shows Westmont Heights between Windsor Avenue and Denver Avenue and the blocks east of Denver along E. Melrose Avenue and E. Emerald Avenue, with Albany Avenue and Maple Avenue to the south; the blocks between Albany and Maple are lettered as the J. A. McCaulay Plan. The housing is almost entirely frame dwellings with a few garages and coops, many lots still empty. The east side of the strip is bounded by the dash-dot line of the Borough of Haddonfield, and Maple Avenue at the bottom runs along the line between Haddon Township and Haddonfield. Water pipes of 2, 4 and 6 inches and fire hydrants are marked in the streets. The upper part has no exposure toward the key map, which occupies the rest of the sheet.
notes: The diagonal stretch of Windsor Avenue (Road) in the upper part, crossed by Utica Avenue, follows today's Coles Mill Road; Windsor Avenue in the lower part is still Windsor Avenue.
The railroad on the west edge is labelled P.R.R. (Delaware River Bridge Route); its line is used today by PATCO and the Atlantic City Line.
Nelson Johnson Cement Block Company beside the railroad.

Map, 100 ft. Title, key map of the town (700 ft to an inch), water facilities text and street index on the right; the map is the L-shaped strip left of and below the heavy line: Windsor Av (Rd) and the P.R.R. (Delaware River Bridge Route) on the left, Utica Av at top, Westmont Heights (E Melrose, E Emerald, Albany, Maple Av, Denver Av) and the J.A. McCaulay Plan at bottom, Haddonfield line on the right.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 covers the eastern centre of Westmont from Elgin Avenue south to N. Atlantic Avenue and the West Jersey and Seashore Railway, between Center and Wynnewood Avenue on the west and Windsor Avenue (Road) and the Pennsylvania Railroad's Delaware River Bridge Route on the north-east. The streets running across it are Elgin, Melrose, Emerald, Virginia, Highland and Haddon Avenue, crossed by Toledo, Locust, E. Crystal Lake, Elm, Stoy and Carlton Avenue, with Maple Avenue cutting diagonally to Haddon Avenue and W. Crystal Lake and Glenwood Avenue south of Haddon. The northern blocks are lettered Westmont Annex and Westmont Annex No. 3, and the triangle between E. Crystal Lake Avenue and Locust Avenue is the J. P. Fowler Plan. Building is mostly frame dwellings, denser along Emerald and Virginia Avenue and on Haddon Avenue. Notable buildings are the First M. E. Church on Center at Emerald Avenue, the Westmont Fire Co. No. 1 firemen's hall at Center and Highland Avenue, the Morgan Bros. Laundry beside it, a row of brick dwellings on Wynnewood Avenue, a gasoline station at Carlton Avenue and a small waiting station of the West Jersey and Seashore Railway at W. Crystal Lake Avenue. Much of the land between Virginia and Highland Avenue is still in large undivided lots. Water pipes and hydrants are shown in all streets. The top-right corner of the sheet is an inset, described separately.
notes: Center (Av.) is Center Street today.
Toledo is Toledo Avenue and South Toledo Avenue today.
The junction of Haddon Avenue with E. and W. Crystal Lake Avenue was rejected by the fit (about 15 m); Melrose Avenue at Toledo was rejected too (about 17 m).
Windsor Avenue (Road) as drawn lies about 40 m west of today's Windsor Avenue in this stretch and was left out of the fit.
Morgan Bros. Laundry and Westmont Fire Co. No. 1 firemen's hall on Center Street at Highland Avenue.

Map, 100 ft. Main: Elgin to Haddon/N Atlantic between Center/Wynnewood and Windsor Av: Toledo, Locust, E Crystal Lake, Elm, Stoy, Carlton, Maple Av, Westmont Annex No 3, Winton plan, J.P. Fowler plan. Part 2: inset at top right, Haddon Av east of Carlton with Belz & Parr Cement Block Works, P.R.R. and W.J.&S.S. R.R., Haddonfield line.

sheet-2-2.description: An inset in the top-right corner of sheet 2, drawn at the same 100 ft scale but turned about ten degrees against the main map. It continues Haddon Avenue east from the main sheet (the key number 2 at its west end marks the join) to the Pennsylvania Railroad's Delaware River Bridge Route and the line of the Borough of Haddonfield. North of Haddon Avenue is an empty triangle belonging to sheet 6 of the key; south of it, in block B, are four frame dwellings numbered 338 to 342 and the Belz & Parr Cement Block Works, a concrete block building with power and lights by electricity. The tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad cross the bottom of the inset, with sheet 7 beyond. The east side is marked no exposure. The inset has no street junction; it is placed by the crossing of Haddon Avenue and the Delaware River Bridge Route and the direction of Haddon Avenue.
notes: Belz & Parr Cement Block Works.
Placed from one hand-picked point (Haddon Avenue at the railroad, today North Haddon Avenue at the Atlantic City Line and PATCO) and a derived point along Haddon Avenue; low confidence.

Map, 100 ft. Main: Elgin to Haddon/N Atlantic between Center/Wynnewood and Windsor Av: Toledo, Locust, E Crystal Lake, Elm, Stoy, Carlton, Maple Av, Westmont Annex No 3, Winton plan, J.P. Fowler plan. Part 2: inset at top right, Haddon Av east of Carlton with Belz & Parr Cement Block Works, P.R.R. and W.J.&S.S. R.R., Haddonfield line.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the north end of Westmont, drawn with north at the top, between Alton Avenue on the west and Locust Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad's Delaware River Bridge Route on the east, from Coopers Creek in the north to Elgin Avenue in the south. Coopers Creek winds across the top of the sheet as the line between Delaware Township and Haddon Township, with the Kronberger Farm buildings in open land to the north-west. The streets are laid out on a skewed grid: Trevor, Vesper, Geneva, Akron and Utica Avenue and Township Drive run south-east, crossed by Cooper, Saginaw, Oneida and Center, with Alton Avenue on the west edge and Elgin Avenue along the south. The blocks are lettered Westmont Annex No. 2, and a narrow strip along Locust Avenue at the east edge is Westmont Annex No. 3. Building is light: scattered frame dwellings with garages, a few brick or concrete block houses, and many vacant lots, especially in the northern blocks around Trevor Avenue and Saginaw. Water pipes and hydrants are shown in the main streets. Block letters run from E and F in the east to S and T in the north. The railroad crosses the creek on a bridge at the east edge. The bottom margin marks the join with sheets 2 and 4 and the end of Toledo Street.
notes: Cooper is Cooper Street and Center is Center Street today.
Trevor Avenue and Township Drive are not in today's street data.
The street lines west of Cooper continue Geneva and Akron Avenue; Akron is offset across Cooper.

Map, 100 ft. North end: Alton, Cooper, Saginaw, Oneida, Center, Locust Av; Trevor, Vesper, Geneva, Akron, Utica, Elgin Av, Township Drive; Cooper Creek and Kronberger Farm at top, P.R.R. (Delaware River Bridge Route) at right.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Westmont from Elgin Avenue south to N. Atlantic Avenue and the railroad, between Alton and Albertson Avenue on the west and Center and Wynnewood Avenue on the east. Elgin, Melrose, Emerald and Virginia Avenue run across the northern half, crossed by Cooper, which turns south-west below Emerald Avenue toward Haddon Avenue; the southern half is cut diagonally by Haddon Avenue, with Albertson, Sunset, E. Walnut and Reeve Avenue north of it and French, Lindisfarne, W. Walnut, W. Chestnut and Wynnewood Avenue south of it. The northern blocks are lettered Westmont Annex. It is a residential district of frame dwellings, with brick dwellings in a row on Wynnewood Avenue and small stores and garages along Haddon Avenue. Institutions and works shown are the Westmont Public School on Reeve Avenue at Haddon Avenue with a separate school room, the Grace Baptist Church, the American Legion Hall and Haddon Township tax office, the Westmont Garage on Haddon Avenue at Cooper, and the Paul & Russell cast stone works beside the railroad at Albertson Avenue. A large empty tract lies south of Haddon Avenue between Albertson and W. Walnut Avenue. The blank area on the west belongs to sheet 5, whose street ends are sketched in. The Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore) runs along the bottom between N. and S. Atlantic Avenue.
notes: Cooper is Cooper Street, Center is Center Street, Reeve Avenue is Reeves Avenue, Sunset Avenue is Sunset Lane and W. Chestnut Avenue (Apple Avenue) is Chestnut Avenue today.
Lettered plan names along Cooper and Albertson Avenue are only partly legible and are left out.
Westmont Public School, Grace Baptist Church, American Legion Hall with the Haddon Township tax office, Westmont Garage, Paul & Russell cast stone manufacturing.

Map, 100 ft. Centre: Elgin to N Atlantic Av between Alton/Albertson and Center/Wynnewood: Cooper, Reeve, E and W Walnut, W Chestnut, Albertson, French, Melrose, Emerald, Virginia, Sunset, Haddon, Lindisfarne Av; Westmont Public School, Grace Baptist Church.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the north-west corner of Westmont, the newly laid out French Estate between the Collingswood borough line and Emerald Avenue, drawn turned so that north points to the upper right. Cuthbert Blvd runs diagonally up the middle of the sheet and curves north at its upper end; parallel to it run Penn Avenue, Addison Avenue, Strawbridge Avenue and Stratford Avenue, crossed by Oriental Avenue, with Linden Avenue at the Collingswood line on the west. In the north-east corner Hampton Road, Emerald Avenue and Bradford Avenue surround the Haddon Township Public School No. 5, a brick school with steam heat and electric light. The south-east part is laid out along Oriental, Virginia and Emerald Avenue, which bend south to Cambridge Road at the bottom, and Haddon Avenue and French Avenue cross the south-west corner. The district is mostly lots without buildings: the frame dwellings are concentrated along Penn Avenue, on Strawbridge and Stratford Avenue, and along Cambridge Road, with a store and a filling station near Haddon Avenue. Many blocks are numbered (102 to 122) by the key map rather than lettered. The north and east edges are marked no exposure. Water pipes are shown only in some streets, and a few fire hydrants.
notes: Cuthbert Blvd is East Cuthbert Boulevard and Cambridge Rd is Cambridge Avenue today.
Haddon Township Public School No. 5 between Emerald Avenue and Bradford Avenue.
Virginia Avenue at Cambridge Road and Emerald Avenue at Strawbridge and Stratford Avenue were rejected by the fit (9 to 14 m): the curving streets of the plan differ from the ones built.

Map, 100 ft. Northwest: Cuthbert Blvd, Penn, Addison, Oriental, Strawbridge, Stratford, Virginia, Emerald, Bradford Av, Hampton Rd, Cambridge Rd; Haddon Township Public School No 5; Collingswood line at left.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6 covers the south-west of Westmont below the railroad, between Cuthbert Avenue on the Collingswood borough line and W. Walnut Avenue, Albertson Avenue and Websters Lane on the east. At the top the Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore) runs between N. Atlantic and S. Atlantic Avenue, with the small Cuthbert station at Cuthbert Avenue. South of S. Atlantic Avenue a grid of Park Avenue, Stokes Avenue and French Avenue holds blocks 127 and 128 and lettered blocks N, O, T and U, mostly laid out in narrow lots with frame dwellings concentrated near Cuthbert Avenue and along French Avenue. Below Stokes Avenue the sheet is taken up by Cuthbert Lake and the stream that feeds it, with block 129 largely open land; Maugers Lane leaves Cuthbert Avenue beside the lake, with a few dwellings and an auto paint shop. On the east W. Park Blvd runs south-east from Park Avenue past the head of the lake, and Albertson Avenue runs south-east toward Websters Lane through empty land. West of Cuthbert Avenue only the ends of Stokes, Lynnwood, Belmont and Merrick Avenue in Collingswood are sketched. The Collingswood Borough and Haddon Township line runs along Cuthbert Avenue. The lower-right quarter of the sheet is an inset, described separately.
notes: Cuthbert Av is West Cuthbert Boulevard today; Lynnwood Av is Linwood Avenue.
Albertson Av south-east of W. Park Blvd and Websters Lane are not in today's street data; the short Albertson Avenue between S. Atlantic and Park Avenue is West Albertson Avenue.
Stokes Avenue is drawn offset across Cuthbert Avenue; both junctions were measured and agree with today's two Stokes Avenue nodes.
W. Walnut Avenue at S. Atlantic Avenue was rejected by the fit (about 11 m).
Cuthbert station of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad at Cuthbert Avenue.

Map, 100 ft. Main: south of the railroad between Cuthbert Av and Albertson Av/Websters Lane: S Atlantic, Park, Stokes Av, Maugers Lane, French Av, W Park Blvd, Cuthbert Lake. Part 2: inset at bottom right, Haddon Av to S Atlantic Av between Cuthbert Blvd and French Av (Lindisfarne Av).

sheet-6-2.description: An inset in the lower-right quarter of sheet 6, framed by a heavy line and drawn at the same 100 ft scale and orientation as the main map. It shows the blocks between Haddon Avenue and S. Atlantic Avenue from Cuthbert Avenue (Cuthbert Blvd north of Haddon Avenue) east to French Avenue, the area that the main map of sheet 6 would otherwise leave out, at the south-west corner of Westmont north of the railroad. Block 125 between Haddon and Lindisfarne Avenue has a row of frame dwellings on Lindisfarne, a brick dwelling and a concrete block store building at Cuthbert Avenue and stores at French Avenue; block 126 between Lindisfarne and N. Atlantic Avenue has a regular row of frame dwellings and a concrete block building at the corner of Cuthbert Avenue. The Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore) runs between N. Atlantic and S. Atlantic Avenue at the bottom. The ends of Strawbridge Avenue and Stratford Avenue are shown north of Haddon Avenue, where the area continues on sheet 5. The Collingswood Borough and Haddon Township line runs along Cuthbert Avenue. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in Haddon and Lindisfarne Avenue.
notes: Cuthbert Blvd and Cuthbert Av are East and West Cuthbert Boulevard today.

Map, 100 ft. Main: south of the railroad between Cuthbert Av and Albertson Av/Websters Lane: S Atlantic, Park, Stokes Av, Maugers Lane, French Av, W Park Blvd, Cuthbert Lake. Part 2: inset at bottom right, Haddon Av to S Atlantic Av between Cuthbert Blvd and French Av (Lindisfarne Av).

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 covers the south of Westmont below the railroad, from W. Walnut Avenue east to Stoy Avenue and from S. Atlantic Avenue south to W. Park Blvd and the Haddon Hills Development Co. plan. Along the top the Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore) runs above S. Atlantic Avenue; below it Ardmore Avenue and the broken line of Westmont Avenue cross W. Chestnut, Glenwood and W. Crystal Lake Avenue, with the J. W. Hobensack Estate between Chestnut and Glenwood. A stream crosses the middle of the sheet into Crystal Lake, whose western arm fills the east side below Westmont Avenue. W. Park Blvd curves across the lower half from Albertson Avenue to W. Crystal Lake Avenue, lined by deep narrow lots of a new subdivision, and south of it Websters Lane, Briarwood, Crestwood and Glenwood Avenue run into the Haddon Hills Development Co. plan (blocks 131 to 134, 141) with Brook Avenue. Building is sparse: frame dwellings along Westmont, Ardmore and S. Atlantic Avenue and near Stoy Avenue, and the Harry P. Stoy saw mill with its sheds east of W. Crystal Lake Avenue in block 135. The heavy line across the lower part separates the second part of the sheet, described separately.
notes: W. Chestnut Av is Chestnut Avenue today.
Glenwood Avenue is drawn with a jog at Westmont Avenue and its junctions sat 6 to 8 m off today's line; it was left out of the fit.
Brook Avenue and Websters Lane are not in today's street data.
The fitted scale is about 4 percent larger than the other sheets (4.18 px/ft against about 4.0).
Harry P. Stoy saw mill east of W. Crystal Lake Avenue.

Map, 100 ft. South of the railroad: W Walnut, W Chestnut, Glenwood, W Crystal Lake, Stoy, Carlton, Hazel, Norwood, Oakland Av; Ardmore, Westmont, W Park Blvd, Brook, Linden Av; Crystal Lake, Haddon Hills Development Co plan, Crystal Lake Realty Co plan, Harry P Stoy saw mill; Haddonfield boundary heavy line across the sheet.

sheet-7-2.description: The second part of sheet 7, below the heavy line across the sheet, is a separate block drawn at its own angle with its own north arrow. It lies east of the main part: from the railroad and S. Atlantic Avenue south to Linden Avenue, between Stoy Avenue on the west and Oakland Avenue and the Borough of Haddonfield on the east, with Carlton, Hazel and Norwood Avenue crossing Westmont Avenue in between. Most of it is the Crystal Lake Realty Company plan, laid out in long narrow lots (blocks D to N and Q) with only a handful of frame dwellings, mostly on Stoy Avenue and along Westmont Avenue near Carlton Avenue. The eastern arm of Crystal Lake lies in the south-west corner, with the Chas. Levis property beside it. The dash-dot line of the Borough of Haddonfield and Haddon Township crosses the north-east corner. The key number 2 at the top marks sheet 2 beyond the railroad, and the number 7 at the west end of Westmont Avenue marks the join with the main part of this sheet.
notes: This part is turned about 13 degrees against the main part of the sheet.
Chas. Levis property on Crystal Lake.

Map, 100 ft. South of the railroad: W Walnut, W Chestnut, Glenwood, W Crystal Lake, Stoy, Carlton, Hazel, Norwood, Oakland Av; Ardmore, Westmont, W Park Blvd, Brook, Linden Av; Crystal Lake, Haddon Hills Development Co plan, Crystal Lake Realty Co plan, Harry P Stoy saw mill; Haddonfield boundary heavy line across the sheet.

sheet-8-1.description: The main part of sheet 8 covers the Bluebird Tract in the far north-west of Haddon Township, along the Collingswood borough line, drawn with north toward the upper right. Burrwood Avenue runs up the west side next to the borough line, with Woodlawn and Lincoln Avenue entering from Collingswood; east of it Morgan Avenue and Guilford Avenue run north to Tatem Avenue, and King Avenue sweeps in a curve around the north-east, with Shady Lane between it and Burrwood Avenue. New Jersey Avenue runs along the south, crossed by Harding Avenue and the southern King Avenue. It is a newly built suburban tract: long even rows of frame dwellings, mostly two-storey, on narrow lots facing Burrwood, Morgan and Guilford Avenue and New Jersey Avenue, with small garages behind; only the lots between Shady Lane and King Avenue are still largely empty. North of the tract is open land with a few buildings of J. W. Richards, including greenhouses. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in Burrwood, Tatem and New Jersey Avenue. The north, east and south margins are marked no exposure. The top-right quarter of the sheet is an inset of Sadlertown, described separately.
notes: The curved King Av around the north-east of the tract is South Park Drive today; Woodlawn Av is West Woodlawn Avenue.
Burrwood Avenue at New Jersey Avenue was rejected by the fit (about 16 m); New Jersey Avenue is drawn with a jog there.
J. W. Richards greenhouses north of the tract.

Map, 100 ft. Main: Bluebird Tract, Burrwood, Morgan, Guilford, Harding, King Av, Tatem Av, Shady Lane, New Jersey Av, Woodlawn, Lincoln Av; Collingswood line at left. Part 2: inset at top right, Sadlertown (Mill St, 1st St, 2nd St, Kurz St, Atlas St, Rhoades Av, Glenwood Av).

sheet-8-2.description: An inset in the top-right quarter of sheet 8, framed by a heavy line, showing Sadlertown, a small settlement south of Westmont near the Haddonfield line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north straight up and no exposure on any side. Mill St runs along the top to Glenwood Av at the north-east corner; Rhoades Av runs south from it, crossed by 1st St and 2nd St, which are only 15 to 20 ft wide. Kurz St and Atlas St, both marked arbitrary (unofficial names), run south-west and south through block 147, a large irregular tract of long lots. Buildings are frame dwellings with sheds, a coloured chapel with stove heat and oil light on Rhoades Av, a coloured Baptist church on Kurz St and a coloured school building in open land to the west. Much of the tract is still open or lightly built. Its position is fixed only by two hand-picked points on Rhoades Av.
notes: Rhoades Av is Rhoads Avenue, Mill St is Macarthur Boulevard and 1st St is First Street today; 2nd St, Kurz St and Atlas St are not in today's street data.

Placed from two hand-picked points on Rhoads Avenue (at Macarthur Boulevard and First Street), 45 m apart; low confidence. Glenwood Av at Mill St falls about 7 m short of today's Glenwood Avenue / Macarthur Boulevard on this placement.
Coloured chapel, Baptist church and school.

Map, 100 ft. Main: Bluebird Tract, Burrwood, Morgan, Guilford, Harding, King Av, Tatem Av, Shady Lane, New Jersey Av, Woodlawn, Lincoln Av; Collingswood line at left. Part 2: inset at top right, Sadlertown (Mill St, 1st St, 2nd St, Kurz St, Atlas St, Rhoades Av, Glenwood Av).
